result.rationale: The diff adds `group.users.delete(user_id)` in remove_member with no rescue; for a has_many :through association, AR's CollectionAssociation#delete looks up the record within the association scope and raises ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound when the id isn't a current member, bypassing the intended `render_json_error` path. The double-click/race scenario is realistic and the client-side `removeMember` in group.js has no failure handler. Mechanism is plausible and grounded in the added code; AR internals can't be fully verified from the diff alone.

judged_text: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:90 — `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a `has_many :through` association internally does `scope.find(user_id)` restricted to current members (verified against installed activerecord 4.1.16 source: `CollectionAssociation#delete` calls `find(records)` when given an id), so it raises an unrescued `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound` instead of the intended graceful `render_json_error` whenever `user_id` is not currently a member of the group (e.g. a resubmitted/double-clicked remove request or a race with a concurrent removal), returning a non-JSON error response the client-side `removeMember` promise (which has no failure handler in admin-group.js.es6) silently swallows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member` which does `group.users.delete(user_id)` before the `if group.save ... else render_json_error` branch. There is no rescue around the delete call, so if the association delete raises (e.g., when `user_id` is not currently in `group.users` due to a double-submit/race), the controller will error out before returning the intended JSON response. This is a correctness/robustness issue in the newly added endpoint, and the client-side `removeMember` action has no explicit failure handling.
